run.question: Use the custom-crd runbook and check why custom CRD whale-watcher resources are not being reconciled by the operator in namespace app-96

report.summary: The requested runbook could not be used: fetch_skill('custom-crd') returned KNOWLEDGE_NOT_FOUND and the only approved runbook for this target is 'service-troubleshooting', so no custom-CRD checklist steps were available to follow. Investigation of namespace app-96 with the Kubernetes tools found the CRD whalewatchers.ocean.io (group ocean.io, kind WhaleWatcher, namespaced, v1 served+stored, Established=True) and a single operator workload, Deployment whale-operator, 1/1 ready, running image python:3.9-slim with command python /app/operator.py and its code mounted from Secret whale-operator, using ServiceAccount whale-operator. That ServiceAccount is bound by ClusterRoleBinding whale-operator to ClusterRole whale-operator, whose only rule is apiGroups ocean.io / resources whalewatchers / verbs get,list,watch — read-only, with no update or patch verb on whalewatchers or whalewatchers/status and no write permission on any other resource. The CRD schema defines status.phase, status.observationCount and status.lastSeen but declares no subresources entry, i.e. no status subresource. The likely cause of the missing reconciliation is therefore an authorization/config gap: the operator can watch WhaleWatcher objects but has no granted verb that lets it persist reconciliation results, so status would never be written; this remains a hypothesis because no 403/Forbidden response, no reconcile failure event and no application log line was observed. The operator pod itself is not crashed (Running, Ready, restartCount 0, no waiting state, no Evicted/OOM marks), and app-96 is a freshly created namespace (created 2026-11-22T09:26:43Z, operator Deployment/ReplicaSet/pod created 09:26:43–09:26:45Z), so its first start in this window is setup, not impact. Prometheus and Jaeger were unreachable (SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), the WhaleWatcher custom resources themselves are not readable with the available tools, the operator's Secret is unreadable, and its container returned no log lines.

claims.text: CRD whalewatchers.ocean.io exists: group ocean.io, kind WhaleWatcher, scope Namespaced, single version v1 (served=true, storage=true, conversion strategy None), storedVersions [v1], with conditions NamesAccepted=True (NoConflicts) and Established=True set at 2026-11-22T09:26:43Z.

The whalewatchers.ocean.io CRD schema defines spec (depth, location, whaleType) and status (lastSeen, observationCount, phase), but the CRD spec returned contains no subresources entry, i.e. there is no status subresource for WhaleWatcher.

ClusterRole whale-operator (created 2026-11-22T09:26:43Z, no aggregationRule) contains exactly one rule: apiGroups ["ocean.io"], resources ["whalewatchers"], verbs ["get","list","watch"] — no update/patch/delete verb on whalewatchers, no whalewatchers/status resource, and no rule for any other resource kind.

ClusterRoleBinding whale-operator binds ServiceAccount whale-operator in namespace app-96 to ClusterRole whale-operator (only subject), so the operator's effective permissions on WhaleWatcher objects are limited to the read verbs of that ClusterRole.

Deployment whale-operator in app-96 (created 2026-11-22T09:26:43Z) has desired/ready/available replicas 1/1/1 with conditions Available=MinimumReplicasAvailable and Progressing=NewReplicaSetAvailable; its pod template runs a single container named operator with image python:3.9-slim, command ["python","/app/operator.py"], env OPERATOR_NAMESPACE from fieldRef metadata.namespace, serviceAccountName whale-operator, and a volume operator-code sourced from Secret whale-operator mounted at /app; no readiness/liveness probe is defined.

Pod whale-operator-5f695b7c66-z9285 in app-96 is Running and Ready (all conditions True), owner ReplicaSet whale-operator-5f695b7c66, node opspilot-m1-control-plane, container operator running since 2026-11-22T09:26:45Z with restartCount 0, empty lastState and no waiting reason.

Namespace app-96 was created 2026-11-22T09:26:43Z, and in the same second Deployment whale-operator recorded 'Scaled up replica set whale-operator-5f695b7c66 from 0 to 1' (ScaledReplicaSet) with a ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate, followed by Pod Scheduled 09:26:43, Created/Pulled 09:26:44 and Started 09:26:45 — i.e. the operator started for the first time in this fresh namespace inside the window.

All 7 events returned across all namespaces for the window are setup/scaling events for app-96 plus one Warning on an Endpoints object named orca ('Failed to create endpoint for service app-95/orca: endpoints "orca" already exists', endpoint-controller, 2026-11-22T09:21:00Z); none of the returned events involves a WhaleWatcher object or a reconcile failure of the whale-operator.

The operator workload itself is not in a failing pod state: pod whale-operator-5f695b7c66-z9285 is Running/Ready with restartCount 0 and no waiting reason, no Evicted or OOMKilled mark, and Deployment whale-operator reports 1 ready/1 available replica, so a crash-loop or eviction of the operator is not the explanation observed.

Rejected: that the WhaleWatcher CRs are unreconciled because the operator container keeps crashing or restarting. The pod shows restartCount 0, state running since 2026-11-22T09:26:45Z, lastState empty and no previous container instance exists, and the Deployment is 1/1 ready.

Primary candidate: ClusterRole whale-operator grants the operator's ServiceAccount only get/list/watch on ocean.io whalewatchers, so any reconcile that must write the WhaleWatcher's status (phase, observationCount, lastSeen) or spec is denied; the reconcile result can never be persisted and the CRs stay un-reconciled even though the operator pod is healthy. Supported by the read-only rule set and the read-only binding, but no 403/Forbidden response or reconcile error line was observed, so the mechanism is inferred, not witnessed.

Second candidate: the CRD declares no status subresource, so an operator implementation that PATCHes/updates whalewatchers/status would fail (subresource not found) independently of RBAC; the correct write path for this CRD would be the main whalewatchers resource, which the ClusterRole also does not allow.

Third candidate that could not be excluded: the operator's program and configuration live in Secret whale-operator (mounted at /app, secret-backed volume), which cannot be read in this Run; a missing/wrong script, wrong watch scope or wrong client configuration inside that Secret could equally prevent reconciliation.

The absence of any reconcile-failure Event is not proof that reconciles succeeded: the operator's ClusterRole grants create on no resource, so it could not record Events about its own failures, and no line from the container was observed to contradict that.

Verify the write path and fix it: grant the whale-operator ServiceAccount update/patch on whalewatchers (and, if a status subresource is added to the CRD, on whalewatchers/status) plus create on events, then confirm the reconcile by re-reading the WhaleWatcher objects' .status.

Before editing anything, reproduce the denial non-destructively with an authorization check from the operator identity (kubectl auth can-i update whalewatchers.ocean.io --as=system:serviceaccount:app-96:whale-operator -n app-96) and run the operator locally against the cluster or with PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 so its reconcile/error output is visible; the current container produced no log lines.

gaps: The requested runbook 'custom-crd' is not an approved runbook of this target: fetch_skill returned KNOWLEDGE_NOT_FOUND, and the only available runbook was 'service-troubleshooting'; therefore none of the custom-CRD runbook steps could be executed and none can be reported as checked.

The WhaleWatcher custom resources themselves could not be read: the Kubernetes tools available accept only the fixed built-in kind list (no custom resource kind), so it is unknown whether any WhaleWatcher objects exist in app-96, what their spec is, and what their .status contains — the 'not reconciled' symptom is taken from the question, not observed here.

fetch_pod_logs for container operator of whale-operator-5f695b7c66-z9285 returned zero lines (view status no_data; no previous container instance exists), so no reconcile attempt, 403/Forbidden or traceback was observed; an empty view is not evidence of absence, and Python stdout buffering (image python:3.9-slim without PYTHONUNBUFFERED) could also hide output.

Secret whale-operator (the operator's code/config source and the deployment's volume) cannot be read, so the program logic, watch configuration and whether it ever attempts a write could not be verified.

Prometheus was unreachable for all metric queries (get_metric_names and execute_prometheus_instant_query returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE) and Jaeger likewise (traces_list_services SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE); no metric or trace evidence about the operator or any whale-operator metric was obtainable, so such series are unknown, not zero.

No observed authorization denial exists in the evidence: the RBAC conclusion is inferred from the verbs granted to ClusterRole whale-operator, not from a recorded 403 response, an apiserver audit entry, or an operator log line.
The CRD's status subresource absence is known from the CRD spec, but whether the operator writes via /status or the main resource could not be determined without the code.

Queries for Services, Endpoints, Roles, RoleBindings and NetworkPolicies returned nothing (several with status no_data), so absence of a Service/NetworkPolicy in app-96 and cluster-wide cannot be asserted as fact, and an egress/DNS block on the operator's apiserver access could not be ruled out or confirmed.
The change history integration is not available in this Run, so who created or last modified the whale-operator Deployment, ClusterRole, ClusterRoleBinding and Secret, and when, is unknown.

Background restarts in other namespaces (kube-system, otel-demo pods show exit 255 'Unknown' around 08:04 and restarts 2-6) were not tied to app-96 and were not treated as impact; no owner-level check of those workloads was performed.
next_steps: Check authorization explicitly for the operator identity: kubectl auth can-i list whalewatchers.ocean.io and kubectl auth can-i update whalewatchers.ocean.io --as=system:serviceaccount:app-96:whale-operator -n app-96, then compare with what the operator code actually attempts.

Inspect the WhaleWatcher objects in app-96 with a custom-resource-capable client (kubectl get whalewatchers.ocean.io -n app-96 -o yaml) to see whether .status is empty/stale and whether resourceVersion or generation changes on reconcile.
Read Secret whale-operator (operator.py) in a controlled, authorized session to confirm the reconcile write path (main resource vs /status) and the watched group/version.
If the reconciler does write status, either add a status subresource to the whalewatchers.ocean.io CRD or grant update/patch on the main resource, and add create on events so failures become visible.
Re-run with PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 or a logging sidecar so operator output is observable, and re-check events for a WhaleWatcher-related Warning afterwards.
Restore Prometheus and Jaeger availability for this target to allow metric/trace corroboration of operator activity.
